item.title: Diversification Across Predictors: Heterogeneous Ensemble Learning for Cross-Sectional Return Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2611.12389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-sectional stock return prediction remains challenging due to extremely low signal-to-noise ratios, high-dimensional factor spaces, and non-stationary predictor effectiveness. Individual model classes exhibit complementary failure modes in this regime: neural networks overfit noise due to high variance, while linear models underfit nonlinear structure due to high bias. We propose a heterogeneous ensemble framework that extends the financial principle of diversification to the predictor level. Through a bagging procedure combining linear predictors with nonlinear predictors, each model functions as a distinct specialist whose prediction errors exhibit low cross-covariance, enabling error cancellation upon aggregation. We formalize this mechanism via bias-variance-covariance decomposition, establishing an exact mathematical correspondence between portfolio diversification and predictor aggregation. On CSI300 daily-frequency Alpha158 factor datasets, the proposed ensemble achieves a Rank IC improvement exceeding 13\% over standalone neural networks and surpasses tree-based state-of-the-art methods including XGBoost and Double Ensemble, as measured by both predictive accuracy and portfolio-based evaluation metrics.
item.dc:creator: Danning Li

item.title: Trained, Frozen, or Absent: Identifying What a Quantum Layer Contributes to Cross-Sectional Equity Ranking
item.description: arXiv:2611.10801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hybrid quantumclassical models are increasingly proposed for nancial prediction, but reported gains are rarely separated from the classical components around them. We study a hybrid quantum temporal convolutional network for daily cross-sectional ranking of 2000 Tokyo Stock Exchange equities under a protocol built to make the quantum contribution identiable: six conditions (circuit trained, frozen or absent, a parameter-matched classical surrogate, and the circuit alone, trained or frozen) through one code path; four walk-forward folds with ve seeds; bootstrap intervals, Deated Sharpe Ratios, backtest-overtting probabilities and family-wise error control; ve classical baselines including a gradient-boosted tree; and a locked holdout. On 500 out-of-sample days two one-sided tests place the trained-versus-frozen dierence inside 0.03 annualised Sharpe (p = 0.0055, minimum detectable eect 0.02): the circuit is equivalent to a frozen one, not merely indistinguishable from it. With the circuit as the head's only input the two are equivalent inside 0.25; against the network with no circuit the design resolves only 0.50. No condition is distinguishable from zero (best De-ated Sharpe Ratio 0.17). The holdout reproduces the ablation on a protable window, and 2000 US equities reproduce it where every condition loses money.
item.dc:creator: Chi-Sheng Chen, Xinyu Zhang, En-Jui Kuo, Rong Fu, Qiuzhe Xie, Fan Zhang

item.title: Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning for an Options Market Maker: An Empirical Study with Real S&P 500 Options
item.description: arXiv:2611.10956v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Options market makers absorb client order flow and must hedge the resulting inventory risk under trading frictions. We study whether an option hedging reinforcement learning (RL) agent trained on historical market data outperforms three alternatives in tail-risk protection: (i) traditional delta hedging, (ii) simple hedge-ratio rules, and (iii) the same agent trained in simulated markets. Most RL hedging agents are trained in model-generated markets that do not capture the crashes and volatility regimes present in real data. We introduce an empirical replay environment using S&P 500 option data from 1996 to 2017 and compare against a matched geometric Brownian motion (GBM) environment, a stochastic-volatility (SABR) simulator, and a hybrid that values historical paths with Black-Scholes, all sharing the same portfolio mechanics, stochastic arrivals, costs, and test period. We train a distributional Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) agent and evaluate it out of sample over 2018-2023. The agent trained on empirical data reduces Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) tail loss by 3.1% compared to delta hedging and outperforms every hedge-ratio rule chosen during the training period and every alternative training environment. The reduction reaches 8.9% in volatile and falling markets, but reverses to a cost of 7-10% in rising markets. Empirical training induces a state-dependent short net delta: the policy under-hedges negative-delta books, most strongly after prices have fallen. This tilt disappears with GBM training and is weaker with SABR or hybrid training. These findings suggest that exposure to historical market dynamics can materially change a tail-risk hedging policy, although the evidence rests on a single test path and the edge is regime-conditional.
item.dc:creator: Jacky Chen, Ing-Haw Cheng, John Hull, Landis Li, Zissis Poulos, Justin Shi, Andreas Veneris, Zeyu Wang

item.title: Optimal execution in a fractional setting with reinforcement learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.11373v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the problem of optimal liquidation with linear market impact, as in the seminal work of Almgren and Chriss, but with an asset driven by a fractional Brownian motion. For $H \neq 1/2$, we observe that the deterministic solution given by Almgren and Chriss is no longer optimal. We develop a strategy to exploit the information induced by the correlation between price increments. The strategy is derived from a policy gradient algorithm, parameterized by a neural network, trained to maximise the CARA utility, for which our method allows for significant improvements.
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Garcin, Jiang Pu, Thomas Verrier

item.title: Adjoint Kernel Sensitivity of the Rough Heston Characteristic Exponent
item.description: arXiv:2611.11652v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-factor approximations of rough volatility kernels affect the characteristic exponents used in Fourier-based derivative valuation. We derive an adjoint representation for the first-order sensitivity of the rough Heston characteristic exponent with respect to its memory kernel, with model parameters and the input variance curve held fixed. The Volterra--Riccati functional $\mathcal L_T(K,z)$ admits a local real-analytic extension, jointly in the kernel perturbation and the transform parameter. The Fr\'echet derivative of this extension with respect to the kernel in $L^1$ is represented by integration against a continuous sensitivity kernel $B_K(u,z)$, obtained from a backward linear Volterra equation and independent of the perturbation direction. This representation resolves the leading-order contributions of kernel perturbations across memory lags. On the structural kernel class, which contains the fractional kernel and its multi-factor approximations and has empty interior in $L^1$, the extension yields Hadamard directional differentiability and a first-order expansion with a quadratic $L^1$-remainder for all sufficiently close structural kernels, uniformly on compact subsets of the strip of transform parameters. The same sensitivity kernel yields multi-factor weight and decay-rate derivatives. Numerical experiments at multi-factor reference kernels assess the finite-resolution implementation and illustrate how the lag distribution of positive perturbations with equal $L^1$ mass affects the first-order response.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Escudero, Francisco J. Luguera-Par\'uas, Miguel Sama

item.title: Generative AI, Managerial Expectations, and Economic Activity
item.description: arXiv:2410.03897v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using generative AI, we extract managers' economic expectations from over 120,000 corporate conference call transcripts. The resulting AI Economy Score predicts GDP growth, production, employment, and wages five or more quarters ahead, beyond survey forecasts and other existing measures. Industry- and firm-level scores capture sector- and firm-specific activity, and a composite of firm, industry, and macroeconomic expectations further improves forecasting power and horizon. Predictability concentrates among historically more accurate, less biased managers, consistent with an information rather than a noise channel. Managerial expectations thus offer incremental insights into economic activity, with implications for macro- and microeconomic decision-making.
item.dc:creator: Manish Jha, Jialin Qian, Michael Weber, Baozhong Yang

item.title: Implied Volatility Expansions for VIX Options in Forward Variance Models
item.description: arXiv:2604.25123v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop expansions for the implied volatility of VIX options within the class of forward variance models based on weak-approximation techniques for VIX option prices. In single-kernel models, such as the standard and rough Bergomi models, the expansion is fully explicit, and we prove that its error is of the same order as that of the underlying price approximation. In mixed-kernel models, we propose two expansions. The first one is fully explicit and relies on a Hermite expansion of the price, which we rewrite exactly as a Black-Scholes price with a shifted volatility, up to explicit residual terms. The second one uses the implied volatility of a mixed log-normal proxy, computed numerically, as its zeroth-order term, and we prove that it achieves the same order of accuracy as in the single-kernel case. The resulting formulas yield implied volatilities directly, rather than by inverting approximate option prices.
item.dc:creator: Ying Liao, Ankush Agarwal, Florian Bourgey

item.title: Soft-Radial Projection for Constrained End-to-End Learning
item.description: arXiv:2602.03461v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Constrained end-to-end learning trains neural networks whose outputs must satisfy feasibility constraints, such as resource, budget, or operational limits. While projection and optimization layers guarantee constraint satisfaction, boundary-based projections can introduce unfavorable optimization geometry: regions of the unconstrained output space are mapped to the same active face of the feasible set. This makes the resulting map locally rank-deficient, suppressing gradients in constrained directions and potentially impairing optimization - a bottleneck known as gradient saturation. We propose Soft-Radial Projection (SRP), a differentiable reparameterization layer that maps unconstrained network outputs into the relative interior of a convex feasible set by smoothly rescaling rays from a strictly feasible anchor point. Unlike hard radial or orthogonal projections, the resulting map is one-to-one and has a full-rank Jacobian almost everywhere, while guaranteeing strict feasibility. We prove that constrained networks equipped with SRP retain universal approximation guarantees. For polytopes and balls, the layer admits a closed-form forward pass, while for general convex sets, the ray-boundary intersection reduces to a one-dimensional search. Experiments on decision-focused learning benchmarks demonstrate strong solution quality at low computational cost, with particularly favorable results in portfolio optimization and substantially lower inference latency than differentiable optimization layers in the evaluated settings.
item.dc:creator: Philipp J. Schneider, Daniel Kuhn

item.title: INEUS: Iterative Neural Solver for High-Dimensional PIDEs
item.description: arXiv:2605.06281v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce INEUS, a meshfree iterative neural solver for partial integro-differential equations (PIDEs). The method replaces the explicit evaluation of nonlocal jump integrals with single-jump sampling and reformulates PIDE solving as a sequence of recursive regression problems. Like Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), INEUS learns global solutions over the entire space-time domain, yet it offers a more efficient treatment of nonlocal terms and avoids the computationally expensive differentiation of full PIDE residuals. These features make INEUS particularly well suited for high-dimensional PDEs and PIDEs. Supported by a contraction-based convergence proof for linear PIDEs, our numerical experiments show that INEUS delivers accurate and scalable solutions for various high-dimensional linear and nonlinear examples.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Loup Dupret, Davide Gallon, Patrick Cheridito

item.title: A Formally Verified Library of Mathematical Finance in Lean 4
item.description: arXiv:2606.01356v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe a library of mathematical finance in the Lean 4 proof assistant, built on Mathlib and the BrownianMotion package. Its benchmark records 804 results from the literature, each with a Lean statement, a status, and a published account of what the formalization leaves out: 766 are proved in full, 18 restate an upstream theorem, and 20 are reduced cores that prove less than the result they are named after. The library is about 158,000 lines of Lean, contains no sorry, and a build-time audit pins every library constant that a benchmark proof cites to Lean's three standard axioms. The It\^o integral is constructed rather than assumed. On it the library proves It\^o's formula for C2 functions of It\^o processes as an identity of processes, L\'evy's characterisation, martingale representation, Girsanov's theorem for bounded predictable drifts, which yields a Brownian motion for the filtration when the driver's paths are almost surely continuous, and unique L2 solutions of Lipschitz stochastic differential equations on every horizon. These results reach the contracts a user prices. In a contract language that separates payoffs from models, the Black-Scholes call is replicated by its delta hedge up to every date before maturity, and every fixed-dated contract on the physical Black-Scholes asset has, under the Girsanov measure of a horizon containing its dates, its risk-neutral value. An audit of faithfulness makes the logical status of every claim checkable, and its review has caught what mechanical gates cannot see, including a convergence theorem whose hypothesis could never be satisfied. Nearly all of the mathematics is classical, and what a formal base over it produces is certified unification of known results; two contributed developments, by Robert Martin, address problems the library's own survey had listed as open. The contribution is methodological and infrastructural.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Coelho
